Marathon Petroleum stock fell 3% today, pulling back from a sharp four-day rally that had pushed it up $25 (6%) through November 13th. The decline follows news that Russian crude production has rebounded significantly — output hit 8.73 million barrels a day in October — which the International Energy Agency says has pushed global oil markets into surplus, meaning supply is now outpacing demand. When crude supply grows relative to demand, refiners face tighter margins on their core business.

The broader context is that refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, which is already a high utilization rate with little room to increase throughput. That means Marathon can't easily offset lower margins by processing more oil — the main lever a refiner typically has when profit per barrel shrinks.
